clue.text: Take advantantage of what Italy and India have reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: both country names begin with a capital letter I, so together they have 'capital I's'

explanation.surface: Someone cashing in on news coming out of Italy and India.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misprints 'advantage' as 'advantantage'. Italy and India each begin with a capital I, so they have 'capital I's', which said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit or profit from something is to turn it to one's own capital, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Set up the French seafood

parts.note: to cock something is to set it up or raise it, as a gun's hammer or a hat's brim
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone arranging a French platter of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small edible bivalve shellfish, sold as seafood.

clue.text: Following advertising get aware of straight away

indicators.note: following places the second phrase's letters after the advertising abbreviation

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work
to be on to something is to have become aware of it

explanation.surface: An instruction to act at once after an advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from Spanish and Italian, it is informal English for immediately.

clue.text: The people shooting arrows here in classic Western

definitions.text: The people shooting arrows here in classic Western

parts.words: The people shooting arrows here in classic Western
parts.note: the people shooting arrows are archers, and 'the archers' sit inside the title of the 1956 John Ford Western

explanation.surface: Bowmen appearing in an old cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ARCHERS can be seen inside the title: THE SE-ARCHERS. 'Here in' points to the archers being within the film's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 John Wayne film directed by John Ford is a celebrated classic of the Western genre.

clue.text: Sing merrily being drunk, having consumed litres

indicators.note: something that has consumed another holds it inside, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: lit is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: A tipsy reveller singing after downing several litres.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to sing or speak with a cheerful rising-and-falling rhythm.

clue.text: Steady partner, one from the same place?

parts.note: stable means steady
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A reliable companion who happens to come from one's own home town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: horses from the same racing yard are this, and so are colleagues from one firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a horse trained in the same yard, and by extension a colleague from the same organisation.

clue.text: Port bottle's seal

definitions.meaning: a harbour city in the south of Ireland
the stopper pushed into a wine bottle's neck

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Irish harbour city and the bark stopper of a bottle share the name.

clue.text: Fine material that could give newspaper distinctive stamp

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical speaking for a group
a die is the tool that strikes a distinctive design onto coins or metal

explanation.surface: A fabric that might give a paper its signature look.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer, stiff muslin cotton, a fine lightweight fabric.

clue.text: Island's character is essential element

parts.note: a key (or cay) is a low island, and the possessive adds an S
tone is the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: The nature of an island is what matters most about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The central wedge holding an arch together, hence the vital part on which everything depends.

clue.text: Caught mistress taking tea? One could be lucky

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a mistress is a lover
tea is sold as leaf

explanation.surface: A man caught with his mistress over tea; a chancy affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' just strings the pieces together. A four-leaved clover is the famous lucky charm, so a clover's leaf could be lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A single leaf of clover is proverbially lucky when it is one of four, so it could be a lucky one.

clue.text: Frightful characters appearing regularly in Burghley

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the stately-home name, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Something alarming spotted again and again at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Burghley House is a grand Elizabethan stately home in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful can mean hideous or unpleasant to look at, a synonym of unsightly.

clue.text: Satiric actor masquerading as posh

indicators.note: masquerading means disguised, so the letters appear in another form

explanation.surface: A comic performer pretending to be upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal for upper-class or belonging to the nobility.

clue.text: Device for carrying babies

definitions.meaning: a stretcher or curtained couch on poles for carrying a person
a group of young animals born at one time, such as puppies

explanation.definitionFit: Both the carried couch on poles and a brood of newborn animals share this name.

clue.text: In the red, fashionable music maker

indicators.note: In at the front says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: claret is red wine from Bordeaux
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy instrument bought while overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the red' suggests debt, but 'the red' is the wine and 'In' places the other piece within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-reed woodwind instrument, so something that makes music.

clue.text: Command having entered 9 perhaps

parts.note: someone who has entered is in
the answer to 9 across is a type of motorway interchange, so an example of a road meeting point

explanation.surface: An order issued after joining the motorway at a cloverleaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order requiring someone to do or refrain from something, so an authoritative command.

clue.text: Insist Romans misrepresented in broadcast

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand that Romans were misreported on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In broadcast' places the definition: 'in' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television broadcast is a transmitted programme, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Trained to find ancient coin in rising river

indicators.note: in places the coin within the river's letters
rising in a down entry means the river's name reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a ducat is an old gold coin of Europe

explanation.surface: Someone schooled to spot old coins in a swelling river.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means schooled or trained, a close synonym.

clue.text: Colour newspaper

definitions.meaning: colours are a regiment's flag, so a banner
the Evening ... is a London newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Both a military flag carried as colours and the London daily share this name.

clue.text: Wife fighting to secure high-class sale

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the fighting word wraps the class letter

parts.note: action is fighting, as in seeing action
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A wife battling to win an upmarket auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch auction is a sale where the price starts high and drops until a bidder accepts.

clue.text: Get attached to film publicity brothers brought up

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: Signing up to a movie promoted by a pair of siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, molecules held as a thin layer on a surface are attached to it in this way.

clue.text: Cut energy — that's harsh

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Slashing energy supplies is called cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and stern are synonyms of strict or unsparing.

clue.text: It involves tricks to tighten with spanner

parts.note: to contract is to tighten or draw together
a bridge spans a gap

explanation.surface: Something involving trickery to tighten up using a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' suggests a wrench, but here it is something that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is played in tricks won by partnerships against a bid.

clue.text: See 21
Fairy queen hugged by Greek character

indicators.note: hugged by means held inside, so the queen goes within the Greek letter

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A fairy queen embraced by a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a beautiful fairy or sprite.

clue.text: What may catch something like a fly

definitions.meaning: a device or snare for catching an animal
a fly was a light horse-drawn carriage, like a small two-wheeled gig

explanation.definitionFit: Both a snare for animals and a light two-wheeled horse carriage share this name.

clue.text: Remote inns served soup

indicators.note: served suggests dished up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Isolated country pubs dishing up a bowl of broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick Italian vegetable soup with pasta or rice, an example of soup.

clue.text: Useless English gent

parts.note: a dud is something useless

explanation.surface: A hopeless English gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal American for a man or fellow, a casual word for a gent.

clue.text: In Lib-Dem leader I will replace ace making comeback that can't be beaten

indicators.note: will replace says the I goes where the other letters were taken out

parts.note: Vince Cable led the UK Liberal Democrats from 2017 to 2019

indicators.note: making a comeback means the three letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former Liberal Democrat leader comeback that no rival can stop.
explanation.walkthrough: In VINCE CABLE the run ECA is 'ace' backwards; putting I in its place gives VINCIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Invincible describes someone or something unbeatable, too strong to be defeated.
